name: What drywall finish level do I need for my kitchen?

mainEntity.name: What drywall finish level do I need for my kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Level 4 finish is standard for most kitchen areas, especially walls covered by cabinets, tile backsplashes, or matte paint. It includes taped joints, three coats of compound, and sanding to leave a flat surface. A Level 5 finish adds a thin skim coat of joint compound over the entire board surface to completely equalize texture. Opt for Level 5 if your kitchen features large open wall areas, critical natural lighting from big windows, or if you plan to use semi-gloss or gloss paint that highlights subtle joint imperfections.
acceptedAnswer.description: A Level 4 finish is standard and works well under tile and cabinets. Choose a Level 5 skim coat for open, brightly lit walls or surfaces with gloss paint.
